source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 10: sin(a - b) by the cross product of two unit vectors (book p.283). The book prints + instead of - on the right side. Proof, no key answer.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh trigonometry ka formula hai jo vectors se saabit karna hai.
Idea: ek hi cross product do tareeqon se nikalein aur dono ko barabar rakhein.
Plan: \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) angles par do unit vectors; definition se \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\) aayega aur determinant se right side.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: angles \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) (maan lein \(\alpha > \beta\)).
Saabit karna hai: \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\).
Tareeqa: Example 17 jaisa: \(xy\)-plane mein do unit vectors \(\underline{OA}\) aur \(\underline{OB}\) banayein jo \(x\)-axis ke saath \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) angle banate hain. Dono ka aapas mein angle \(\alpha - \beta\) hai. Cross product ki definition mein \(\sin\) aata hai, isi liye sine ka formula is se nikalta hai.

Dono unit vectors likhein
\[\underline{OA} = \cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underline{j}\]
\[\underline{OB} = \cos\beta\,\underline{i} + \sin\beta\,\underline{j}\]
Kyun: Unit circle (radius 1 wala daira) par angle \(\alpha\) wale point ke coordinates \((\cos\alpha, \sin\alpha)\) hote hain; yahi vector ke components hain. Lambai \(\sqrt{\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha} = 1\), is liye yeh unit vector hai.

Definition se cross product
\[\underline{OB} \times \underline{OA} = (1)(1)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\,\underline{k}\]
\[= \sin(\alpha - \beta)\,\underline{k} \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Dono ki lambai 1 hai, \(\underline{OB}\) se \(\underline{OA}\) tak angle \(\alpha - \beta\) hai. \(\underline{OB}\) se \(\underline{OA}\) ki taraf ghoomna ghari ki sui ke ulat (anticlockwise) hai, is liye right hand rule ka angootha upar, yani \(+\underline{k}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\underline{OA} \times \underline{OB}\) lete to rukh \(-\underline{k}\) hota; tarteeb soch samajh kar chunein.

Wohi cross product determinant se
\[\underline{OB} \times \underline{OA} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ \cos\beta & \sin\beta & 0 \\ \cos\alpha & \sin\alpha & 0 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= \underline{i}(0) - \underline{j}(0)\]
\[+ \underline{k}(\cos\beta\sin\alpha - \sin\beta\cos\alpha)\]
\[= (\sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta)\,\underline{k} \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Dono vectors ka \(\underline{k}\) component 0 hai, is liye \(\underline{i}\) aur \(\underline{j}\) ke minors mein har product mein 0 aata hai. Sirf \(\underline{k}\) wala minor bachta hai.

(1) aur (2) ko compare karein
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
Kyun: Ek hi vector ko do tareeqon se likha; dono barabar hain, is liye \(\underline{k}\) ke coefficients bhi barabar.

Numbers se tasdeeq
\[\alpha = 90^{\circ},\ \beta = 30^{\circ}:\ \sin 60^{\circ} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[(1)\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - (0)\tfrac{1}{2} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) aaya. Kitab wala \(+\) sign lein to \(\alpha = \beta = 45^{\circ}\) par left side \(\sin 0 = 0\) aur right side \(1\) aata, jo mumkin nahi; is se pata chalta hai ke sahi sign minus hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) chhapa hai, jo ghalat hai: plus wali right side to \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) hai. Sahi formula \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) hai, aur cross product yahi saabit karta hai. Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: sine ke formula mein beech ka sign wohi hota hai jo angle mein hai.
